## TL;DR

Polished the mobile web UI across seven reported issues: 44px tap targets in the top bar and on the Agents page, 16px inputs on coarse-pointer devices so iOS does not zoom, touch-only hiding of keyboard hints, a compact icon-only sidebar plus wrapping headers for landscape phones and 768px tablets, a PWA that opens Work with a real iOS icon and free rotation, and a 200-with-null stats response for branchless tasks. Verified with the existing test suite, the UI smoke test, and a throwaway Playwright/WebKit scan that measured every acceptance criterion at 360, 390, 412, 740x360, 844x390, and 768x1024, plus visual screenshots of the phone and landscape layouts.

## Work and rationale

**Tap targets.** The top bar had pointer-sized controls (bell, theme, help, and the repo colour chip at 30–31px, search at 27px). Rather than inflating them only at phone widths, I applied a 44px floor at `max-width: 900px`, which covers portrait phones, landscape phones, and 768px tablets. The repo chip is a colour picker, not a project switcher, so below 720px it becomes an icon-only 44x44 trigger with an explicit `aria-label` that names the repo; its colour swatches and Default button also grow to 44px so the popover is usable. The search pill takes the space the desktop `.spacer` used, with a 44px floor and 44px min-width; the desktop search shortcut chip (`⌘K`) is hidden on touch. NoticeBell/ReminderCards live in scoped styles, so their 44px rules had to be added in those components to beat the scoped originals.

**iOS zoom.** A single last-in-file `@media (pointer: coarse)` block raises `.field input/select/textarea`, `.ff-textarea`, `.nt-body-textarea`, `.search-overlay-input`, and drawer/settings controls to 16px. `.nt-body-textarea` is scoped, so it got its own coarse rule in `TaskDrawer.vue`. A small caret in `TopBar.vue` also keeps `apple-touch-icon` in sync with the chosen repo colour.

**Touch-only hints.** The palette footer, the empty-palette keyboard hint rows, and the top pill's `⌘K` are hidden under `@media (hover: none), (pointer: coarse)`. I included `pointer: coarse` because a touchscreen hybrid can still report hover; the task's literal requirement was `hover: none`. The pill's `data-tip` was simplified to "Search", so no tooltip advertises keyboard commands. This block sits at the very end of `style.css`: an earlier placement silently lost to the base `.search-*` rules defined below it, which the first WebKit scan caught.

**Landscape/tablet layout.** `useResponsiveLayout` intentionally keeps desktop composition at 720px+ (the existing test asserts that), so I did not move the phone breakpoint. Instead, a compact shell applies at `720–900px`: the sidebar becomes a 60px icon-only rail (labels moved into a `.nav-label` span, `aria-label` preserved, decorative foot/theme/build widgets hidden), page headers wrap their actions under the title, and the Work header's inline flex styles were replaced with classes so `.work-header-actions` can take a full row. The Agents sub-tab strip swaps horizontal clipping for wrapping, and phone-width Agents controls get a 44px floor. The section eyebrow (`Default agents` + pricing link + Refresh models) also wraps on phones so the refresh control no longer crowds the pricing link.

**PWA.** Manifest `start_url` is now `/work` and `orientation` is `any`. `/apple-touch-icon.png` (and the precomposed alias) render a 180x180 PNG from the existing icon renderer instead of falling through to the SPA HTML, are linked from `index.html`, and are public routes under auth.

**Stats 404.** `GET /api/tasks/:id/stats` now returns `200 {ok:true, stats:null}` when there are no recorded sessions. The client already typed the payload as nullable and treats null as "no usage yet", so the drawer no longer logs a 4xx for branchless tasks.

## Approaches tried

I first considered switching the app to the phone shell at up to 860px, which would have made the landscape/tablet acceptance trivial. The existing responsive test explicitly keeps desktop composition at 768px and the ADR describes the phone shell as a distinct composition, so that would have been a product change disguised as a bug fix. The compact rail keeps desktop semantics and only removes width the header needs.

For tap targets I initially used one global media block, but several controls are defined in scoped Vue styles where an unscoped rule can never win. Moving the sizing into `TopBar.vue`, `NoticeBell.vue`, and `ReminderCards.vue` fixed that without `!important`.

For hints, my first media block was placed next to the top-bar rules, above the base `.search-overlay-keyboard-hint` rule — same specificity, later source wins, so the legend stayed visible. A real WebKit run showed `display:flex`; moving the block to the end of the stylesheet fixed it. This is exactly the kind of ordering bug a source-only test would miss.

## Challenges and blockers

The remote validation runner runs the full suite, and it surfaced unrelated flakes across retries: a `ui-smoke` failure with no captured output on one run, and `agent-review.test.ts` failing twice in different ways — once with ENOENT / "not a git repository" while its temp repo was torn down, and once timing out while waiting for its review report to appear under load. The same file passed in isolation (17/17) both times, and a clean gate run followed; I did not change review code. Because the branch had drifted 87 commits behind main, I merged main in before the final gate — the merge was conflict-free, and `repoos check --changed main` passed afterwards (the only changed paths are this task's files).

The other challenge was measurement flakiness in my ad-hoc Playwright scan: measuring immediately after `.topbar` appeared occasionally read unstyled boxes (19–22px) on one viewport. Waiting for the built stylesheet to settle (`.theme-toggle` computes to 44px) made three consecutive full scans deterministic. That was a harness race, not an app bug; a QA tap-target scan should wait for layout stability too.

I could not verify a real iOS device's home-screen install or Safari zoom behaviour from this environment. The PWA route/type and the 16px computed sizes were verified in WebKit; iOS install proof needs a real device.

## Key learnings

- Scoped Vue styles beat global CSS regardless of source order; touch sizing for a component belongs in that component's `<style scoped>`.
- Media-query blocks for the same selector must come after the base rule, not just anywhere in the file.
- `pointer: coarse` is the right signal for input font size, but Playwright only emulates it with `hasTouch`; plain viewport resizing does not.
- `@media (hover: none), (pointer: coarse)` is a better touch-hints gate than `hover: none` alone for hybrid devices.
- The existing 720px breakpoint is a deliberate product boundary; layout fixes at 720–900px should add a compact mode, not reuse the phone shell.
